concerns.text: T005 [P] implements `download_data.py` but has an implicit prerequisite of having the SRA Toolkit installed. No task in the plan installs or verifies the presence of the SRA Toolkit, creating a producer‑before‑consumer ordering gap.

T006 [P] runs `preprocess.R` which requires the Seurat v4 R package. The only preceding task that touches the R environment is T002b (system‑level R install), but T002b does not explicitly install or pin the Seurat package, leaving a missing dependency before the consumer task.

The `[P]` tag on T005 assumes the task can run in parallel with other tasks. Since `download_data.py` writes files into the shared `data/raw/` directory, concurrent executions could clash (e.g., two parallel instances trying to download different datasets into the same folder), violating the parallel‑safety guarantee.

T002b is marked `[P]` but performs a system‑wide installation of R and Seurat via a package manager. Parallel execution of multiple `[P]` tasks that also modify the system environment could lead to race conditions or inconsistent environments.
